body_text: – If confirmed by the European Commission, REDEMPLO would be the first and only siRNA medicine authorized in the EU for both genetically confirmed and clinically diagnosed adult patients with FCS – People living with FCS have extremely high triglyceride levels and a substantially higher risk of acute pancreatitis and related long-term complications, often resulting in a reduced quality of life – The CHMP opinion is based on positive results from the Phase 3 PALISADE study where REDEMPLO reduced triglycerides by a median of 80% from baseline and significantly fewer cases of acute pancreatitis were seen in patients using REDEMPLO compared with those using placebo PASADENA, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Apr. 24, 2026-- Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: ARWR) today announced that the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (EMA CHMP) has adopted a positive opinion, recommending the approval of REDEMPLO® (plozasiran), a small interfering RNA (siRNA) medicine, as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglyceride levels in adult patients with familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS). FCS remains widely underdiagnosed and affects an estimated 1 to 13 people per million globally. This rare disease is characterized by triglyceride levels that can be orders of magnitude higher than normal, leading to a substantially higher risk of developing acute, recurrent, and potentially fatal pancreatitis. The European Commission is expected to issue a decision on REDEMPLO’s Marketing Authorization in the second quarter of 2026. If approved, REDEMPLO will be the first and only siRNA medicine authorized in the European Union for both genetically confirmed and clinically diagnosed adult patients with FCS. This recommendation follows approvals in the United States, Canada, and China, as Arrowhead continues its efforts to increase global access to care for people living with FCS. In a press release announcing the positive opinion, EMA stated, "Although other authorised medicines can help people with FCS confirmed by genetic testing, REDEMPLO does not require genetic confirmation of the condition, thus providing a treatment option for more adults with FCS and addressing the unmet medical need in these patients." “We are pleased with the CHMP’s recommendation, which brings us closer to potential approval of REDEMPLO as a new treatment option for people living with genetically or clinically confirmed FCS across Europe,” said Christopher Anzalone, Ph.D., President and CEO at Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals. “This milestone reflects the strength of the clinical data and the ability of our TRiM™ platform to enable targeted siRNA therapies to potentially reach multiple tissues and disease areas. We believe REDEMPLO could represent an important new option for the FCS community in Europe, and we are working with regulators and the healthcare community to bring this therapy to more patients as quickly as possible.” Harnessing Arrowhead’s proprietary Targeted RNAi Molecule (TRiM™) platform, REDEMPLO is designed to silence the mRNA encoding apolipoprotein C-III (apoC-III). ApoC-III is a key regulator of triglyceride metabolism that inhibits triglyceride catabolism and clearance, resulting in elevated triglyceride levels. Individuals with genetic loss-of-function variants in APOC3 typically have markedly lower triglyceride levels and a reduced risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The CHMP positive opinion was supported by clinical data from the Phase 3 PALISADE study, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adults with clinically diagnosed or genetically confirmed FCS. The PALISADE study met its primary endpoint and all multiplicity-controlled key secondary endpoints, including demonstrating significant reductions in triglycerides and apoC-III and in the incidence of acute pancreatitis in the pooled dose groups. In PALISADE, 25 mg REDEMPLO reduced triglycerides by a median of 80% from baseline versus a 17% reduction with placebo and significantly fewer cases of acute pancreatitis were seen in patients using REDEMPLO compared with those using placebo. REDEMPLO is self-administered via subcutaneous injection once every three months.1,2 The most common adverse reactions are hyperglycaemia (12.8%), headache (6.8%), nausea (4.7%), and injection site reaction (4.7%). “Patients with FCS face a substantial burden of disease and are at life-long risk of acute pancreatitis, with few effective treatment options available,” said Gerald F Watts, DSc, PhD, MD, FRCP, Professor of Cardio-metabolic Medicine, University of Western Australia. “The results from the PALISADE study demonstrate that plozasiran can achieve substantial and sustained reductions in triglycerides in patients with FCS. These data highlight the potential of targeted RNA interference approaches in addressing conditions like FCS that have so far been difficult to treat. Plozasiran is a major advance in the care of FCS and a significant step toward expanding treatment options for patients across Europe.” The efficacy and safety results from the PALISADE study were presented at the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Congress 2024 and the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions 2024 (AHA24) and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine and Circulation , respectively. ESC, AHA24, and other plozasiran presentations may be accessed on the Events and Presentations page in the Investors section of the Arrowhead website. REDEMPLO has been granted Orphan Designation by the EMA for the treatment of patients with FCS, and Breakthrough Therapy Designation, Fast Track Designation, and Orphan Drug Designation by the U.S. FDA for the treatment of patients with FCS. About FCS Familial chylomicronemia syndrome (FCS) is a severe and rare disease leading to extremely high triglyceride (TG) levels, typically over 10 mmol/L (880 mg/dL). Such severe elevations can lead to various serious signs and symptoms including acute and potentially fatal pancreatitis, chronic abdominal pain, diabetes, hepatic steatosis, and cognitive issues. Currently, there are limited therapeutic options to adequately treat FCS. About the PALISADE Phase 3 Study The PALISADE study (NCT05089084) was a Phase 3 placebo-controlled study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of plozasiran in adults with genetically confirmed or clinically diagnosed FCS. The primary endpoint of the study was percent change from baseline in fasting TG versus placebo at Month 10. A total of 75 subjects distributed across 39 different sites in 18 countries were randomized to receive 25 mg plozasiran, 50 mg plozasiran, or matching placebo once every three months. Participants who completed the randomized period were eligible to continue in a 2-part extension period, where all participants receive plozasiran. About REDEMPLO® (plozasiran) REDEMPLO (plozasiran) is the first and only siRNA treatment approved in these countries that has been studied in both genetically confirmed and clinically diagnosed patients living with FCS. REDEMPLO is a first-in-class siRNA therapeutic designed to suppress the production of apoC-III, a protein produced in the liver that raises triglyceride levels by slowing their breakdown and clearance. By targeting apoC-III with sustained silencing, REDEMPLO delivers significant reductions in triglyceride levels. REDEMPLO is self-administered via subcutaneous injection once every three months. The EMA CHMP has adopted a positive opinion recommending the European Marketing Authorization of REDEMPLO (plozasiran), which is already approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Health Canada, and China’s National Medical Products Administration as an adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides for adults with Familial Chylomicronemia Syndrome (FCS). In addition to approvals of REDEMPLO in the U.S., Canada, and China, plozasiran has been submitted to additional global regulatory authorities for review and marketing authorization. Plozasiran is also being investigated in the SHASTA-3 ( NCT06347003 ), SHASTA-4 ( NCT06347016 ), and SHASTA-5 ( NCT06880770 ) Phase 3 studies in adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia and the MUIR-3 ( NCT06347133 ) Phase 3 study in adults with hypertriglyceridemia. In December 2025, plozasiran was granted Breakthrough Therapy designation by the U.S. FDA in severe hypertriglyceridemia. title: Scaling the AI Data Center: Silicon Photonics as the Industrial Foundation for Next-Gen Optics
summary: Scaling AI data centers demands better optics. Silicon photonics is leading the shift—delivering the efficiency and scalability needed for 400G → 1.6T networks.
body_text: In the world of optical transceivers, a common question is: “Which is better—electro-absorption modulated laser (EML) or silicon photonics?” It is a useful question for understanding where high-speed optical networking is heading. The short answer is that both technologies have played important roles in the evolution of high-speed optics. AOI has built products using each and was among the first companies to bring EML technology to market. Today, however, much of AOI’s roadmap— from 400G to 800G to 1.6T —is centered on silicon photonics. Not because it is trendy, but because it provides a stronger foundation for scaling and automation. What is EML Technology? EML technology combines a laser and a modulator into a single device. This architecture allows high-speed optical signals to be generated within a compact component. Its integrated structure simplified early product development and helped accelerate the introduction of faster optical modules. EML technology continues to be the "gold standard" for specific applications, particularly long-reach (LR4/ER4) requirements exceeding 10km. Because of its superior "chirp" and dispersion characteristics, EML remains a strong fit where established architectures or specialized long-distance system requirements are the priority. What is Silicon Photonics? Silicon photonics uses silicon and CMOS-style manufacturing processes to build optical components on a chip. A continuous-wave laser feeds the photonic integrated circuit (PIC), which performs modulation, routing, and other optical functions. This design enables a highly integrated optical platform. Because silicon photonics leverages semiconductor manufacturing techniques, it is well suited to support the growing scale of cloud data centers, AI infrastructure, and high-bandwidth networking environments. Silicon Photonics and the Future of High-Speed Optics As networking speeds advance from 400G to 800G and eventually 1.6T optical transceivers, scalability becomes increasingly important. Silicon photonics enables multiple product generations to be built on a shared platform, allowing core design elements and manufacturing processes to evolve more efficiently over time. This platform continuity helps streamline the development of new optical modules while supporting more predictable product roadmaps. For hyperscale data centers and network operators, this consistency can simplify infrastructure planning as network speeds continue to increase. From a performance standpoint, while silicon photonic modulators may have different insertion loss profiles compared to EML, they are the primary enablers for next-generation, low-power architectures. This design flexibility allows for the reduction of overall system power consumption (W/bit) by streamlining the optical path and reducing the reliance on power-intensive signal processing components—a critical requirement for the energy-demanding environments of modern AI data centers. Why AOI’s Roadmap Leans to Silicon Photonics One advantage of silicon photonics is its compatibility with automated manufacturing processes. Rather than redesigning the manufacturing flow for each new speed generation, AOI can carry the same core platform forward from 400G to 800G and beyond. That consistency benefits both engineering teams and customers seeking predictable product ramps and stable roadmaps. The technology also lends itself naturally to automation. Its chip-level integration makes assembly steps more repeatable, which translates into higher yields and faster, more reliable scaling. This is a key factor in AOI’s ability to produce optical components economically at high volume, including in the United States , where automated manufacturing supports shorter and more resilient supply chains. The Next Generation of Optical Connectivity EML continues to have a role in the optical ecosystem, but its role has evolved. Earlier product cycles relied heavily on EML technology because it enabled faster time-to-market. However, as we move toward 1.6T, EML faces a "complexity wall". An 8-channel 1.6T EML module requires eight separate laser chips to be Individually aligned and bonded—a process prone to "yield stacking" risks. Silicon photonics avoids this by using monolithic integration, where one photonic chip handles all channels. Furthermore, silicon photonics is the primary driver behind the transition to CPX (Common Pluggable) platforms and External Laser (ELSFP) architectures. By moving heat-generating lasers away from the sensitive high-density optics and switch ASICs, this approach solves the thermal challenges of modern AI clusters. This "remote laser" design ensures that as we scale to higher bandwidths, the most critical components remain in a stable thermal environment, significantly improving overall system reliability and serviceability. As AI infrastructure and high-performance computing continue to expand, the industry will increasingly rely on technologies that enable scalable and automated production. With its ability to support these demands, silicon photonics is well positioned to drive the next era of high-speed connectivity.

title: How to source candidates: 12 Proven strategies for recruiters
summary: Learn how to source candidates with proven strategies, from AI-powered sourcing and talent rediscovery to referrals, outbound outreach, and community building.
body_text: SJ Niderost Posted on Apr 13 Roughly 70% of the global workforce is passive — they're not actively job searching, scrolling job boards, or submitting applications. These prospective candidates won't come to you, no matter how compelling your strong employer brand or how many jobs you post. The best recruiting teams source proactively across multiple channels to find, engage, and hire top talent before competitors do. Effective candidate sourcing is both art and science. It requires knowing which channels work best for different role types, how to personalize outreach at scale, when to leverage AI versus manual effort, and how to measure what's actually driving hires rather than just application volume. This guide covers 12 proven candidate sourcing strategies organized by type, AI-powered outbound, manual outbound, inbound optimization, and community building, so you know which to use and when. What is candidate sourcing? Candidate sourcing is the proactive process of identifying and engaging potential candidates for current or future job openings, regardless of whether those candidates are actively job hunting. It involves searching databases and professional networks, reaching out to passive candidates, building talent pools for future needs, and nurturing relationships with candidates over time. The data is clear: job boards drive volume, but referrals, internal mobility, and direct sourcing consistently deliver more hires. Sourced candidates are 8x more likely to be hired than inbound applicants. Talent sourcing is distinct from recruiting, which encompasses the full hiring process, including job posting, application review, interviewing, offer management, and onboarding. Sourcing specifically focuses on the top of the funnel, finding qualified candidates and getting them interested in your opportunity before they formally apply. Effective talent sourcing targets both active candidates (currently job searching) and passive candidates (employed and not actively looking but potentially open to the right opportunity). Because passive candidates represent the majority of the talent market and often include the most sought-after professionals, sourcing has become essential, not optional, for competitive hiring. 12 proven candidate sourcing strategies 1. AI sourcing agents What it is: AI that searches across hundreds of millions of candidate profiles to identify matches for your roles, using contextual understanding rather than keyword matching. Modern AI sourcing agents interpret job requirements, evaluate career trajectories, surface candidates with transferable skills, and prevent duplicate outreach by tracking past contact. When it works best: AI sourcing excels for high-volume roles where you need to identify dozens of candidates quickly, hard-to-fill positions requiring creative search strategies, and any scenario where manual talent sourcing can't keep pace with requisition volume. It's particularly effective when integrated with your ATS and CRM, so the AI has complete candidate context. Impact and tips: Teams using AI sourcing agents report handling 40%+ more requisitions without adding recruiting headcount. The key is to provide clear feedback to the AI on which candidates are good or poor matches. This teaches the system to improve its recommendations over time. AI sourcing across 800M+ profile databases also reduces dependency on expensive external recruiters and sourcing site licenses, often delivering significant cost savings. 2. AI-powered talent rediscovery What it is: Using AI to automatically surface past qualified candidates from your ATS and CRM who are strong matches for newly opened roles. This includes silver medalists who interviewed well but weren't quite right for previous positions, past applicants whose experience now aligns with current needs, sourced candidates who weren't ready to move when they were originally contacted, and employee referrals who applied for different roles. When it works best: Talent rediscovery works for virtually every role type and should be your first sourcing strategy before searching externally. These qualified candidates already know your company, have been partially vetted through past interactions, and often convert faster than cold outreach. It's especially effective for roles similar to those you've previously hired for. The value of talent rediscovery compounds as your organization grows. Enterprises with years of candidate relationships and thousands of past applications see dramatically higher ROI than early-stage startups just beginning to build their databases. If you're a smaller organization without an established candidate database, prioritize other talent sourcing channels while building your talent pool for future rediscovery opportunities. Impact and tips: According to recent industry data, 46% of hires at top-performing teams come from existing candidate databases. Without AI, most of this talent sits unused because recruiters lack the time to manually search thousands of past interactions. Set up automated talent rediscovery so the AI proactively surfaces past candidates whenever new requisitions open. This should happen automatically, not as a manual step recruiters remember to do. When re-engaging past candidates, acknowledge the previous interaction and explain why this new role might be a better fit. AI-powered outreach tools can automatically generate personalized messages that reference past applications, interview feedback, or previous conversations, making re-engagement more relevant and less manual. 3. Manual sourcing What it is: Traditional candidate sourcing using Boolean search operators (AND, OR, NOT, parentheses) to build complex search strings on platforms like job boards or resume databases. This manual approach requires recruiters to construct queries such as "(software engineer OR developer) AND python AND (startup OR scale-up) NOT intern" and then manually review hundreds of profiles. When it works best: Boolean sourcing can work for very specific, narrow searches where you need precise control over search criteria, or when you're searching for unique skill combinations that require complex logic. It's also the only option if you're using platforms without AI search capabilities. However, for most modern recruiting needs, manual Boolean sourcing has been superseded by AI-powered alternatives that deliver better results with less effort. Impact and tips: Boolean sourcing is time-intensive and doesn't scale, building effective search strings requires expertise, and manually reviewing profiles is slow. The approach also misses qualified candidates whose profiles use terminology different from your search string. Teams relying primarily on manual Boolean sourcing report spending 60-70% of their time on search and profile review rather than candidate engagement. If you must use Boolean search, save your most effective queries for reuse, combine multiple variations of the same concept (e.g., "machine learning" OR "ML" OR "artificial intelligence"), and use parentheses to group logic properly. However, consider that AI-powered sourcing platforms can search across 800M+ profiles in context, understand semantic meaning beyond keywords, automatically prevent duplicate outreach, and integrate with outreach workflows, typically delivering 5-10x efficiency improvements over manual Boolean searches while finding candidates that keyword matching would miss. 4. Multi-channel outreach sequences What it is: Automated engagement campaigns that reach candidates across multiple channels: email, LinkedIn InMail, SMS, and even phone, using personalized recruitment messaging and timed follow-ups. Rather than a single cold message, candidates receive a sequence of 3-5 touchpoints over 2-3 weeks, each adding value or context. When it works best: Multi-channel sequences dramatically improve response rates for passive candidate outreach. They work across all role types but are particularly effective for competitive talent, where a single message can get lost in crowded inboxes. Personalization is critical. Generic mass messages perform poorly across all channels. Impact and tips: AI-personalized outreach sequences achieve 30-40% higher response rates compared to generic templates. The personalization should reference specific aspects of the candidate's background, such as current company, recent projects, career transitions, or relevant skills. Structure sequences to provide value in each message: the first message introduces the opportunity, the second message shares company content or a team spotlight, and the third message addresses common objections. Test different messaging angles and subject lines to see what resonates. AI can automate this optimization. Avoid aggressive sequences that feel like spam; respect when candidates don't respond rather than escalating contact frequency. 5. GitHub, Stack Overflow, and niche platforms What it is: Sourcing technical talent on platforms where they're professionally active beyond LinkedIn. GitHub shows actual code contributions and projects; Stack Overflow demonstrates problem-solving and community engagement; Dribbble and Behance showcase design portfolios; and industry-specific communities host domain experts. When it works best: This proactive strategy is essential for technical roles (engineering, data science, design) where candidates may not maintain active LinkedIn profiles but are highly engaged in professional communities. It's also effective for finding qualified candidates with demonstrated skills rather than relying solely on resume claims. Impact and tips: Engage with candidates' work before pitching them. Comment on a GitHub project, reference a Stack Overflow answer, or compliment a design on Dribbble. This personalized approach dramatically improves response rates versus cold outreach. Use platform-specific search (search GitHub by programming language, contributions, stars on repositories; search Stack Overflow by tags and reputation). Many technical candidates prefer being contacted via platform messaging or the email listed on their GitHub profile rather than LinkedIn InMail. Respect community norms. Some platforms discourage recruiter activity, so read the room before mass outreach. 6. Employee referrals What it is: Leveraging your current employees' professional networks to source candidates. Employees refer people they've worked with previously or know from their industry, and typically receive a referral bonus if their candidate is hired. When it works best: Employee referrals consistently deliver the highest-quality hires across most organizations and role types. Referred candidates convert at higher rates throughout the funnel, ramp faster after hire, and show better retention. Referrals are particularly effective for cultural fit assessment since employees understand your company and can pre-screen for alignment. Impact and tips: Make the referral process as frictionless as possible. Use simple forms, mobile-friendly submission, and clear visibility into which roles need referrals. Keep referrers updated on their candidate's progress; radio silence discourages future referrals. Consider tiered bonuses based on role difficulty or diversity hiring goals. Proactively ask for referrals rather than waiting. When opening a new role, message employees who previously worked at target companies or have relevant networks. Remember that employee referrals can reduce pipeline diversity if not managed intentionally; balance referrals with other talent sourcing channels to maintain diverse candidate pools. 7. Career site optimization What it is: Treating your company's career site as a high-intent inbound talent sourcing channel by optimizing for search engines, candidate experience, and conversion. Most candidates research your company website before applying, making it a critical touchpoint. When it works best: Career site optimization delivers ongoing passive inbound for all roles. It's especially valuable for employer branding and attracting candidates who are already interested in your company. Strong career sites reduce dependency on expensive job boards and create an owned channel for top tier talent attraction. Impact and tips: For a more bespoke, personalized career site experience that showcases your brand, explore dedicated talent marketing solutions that optimize for SEO by using job titles candidates actually search for (not internal job codes), including location and key skills in page titles and descriptions, and publishing authentic content about team culture and work. Streamline the application process. Every additional step or required field reduces conversion by 10-15%. Feature team spotlights, day-in-the-life content, and employee testimonials that humanize your company. Make it easy to browse all open roles with good filtering and search. Include clear value propositions for why candidates should join. Add chat functionality or FAQs to answer common questions. Track where applicants drop off and optimize those friction points. 8. Job boards (targeted) What it is: Posting jobs to industry-specific, role-specific, or community-specific job boards beyond the major generalist platforms like Indeed and LinkedIn. Examples include AngelList and Wellfound for startups, Dribbble for designers, Dice for tech roles, HigherEdJobs for academic positions, and hundreds of niche boards. When it works best: Targeted job boards reach candidates who self-select into specific communities and are more likely to be qualified for specialized roles. They often have less competition than major boards, where your posting gets buried. Use niche boards for hard-to-fill specialized roles, when targeting specific candidate communities, and when you want higher quality over volume. Impact and tips: Optimize job descriptions for each platform's audience. The tone and format that works on LinkedIn won't necessarily resonate on AngelList or GitHub Jobs. Many niche boards have smaller but highly engaged audiences; don't judge success purely by application volume. Track source effectiveness to identify which boards actually produce hires rather than just generate applications. Some niche boards offer community features (discussions, company events, job fairs) beyond just posting. Engage with these to build visibility. Consider that targeted boards often cost more per posting but deliver better ROI through qualified applicants. 9. Talent communities and nurture campaigns What it is: Building long-term relationships with candidates who aren't ready to move now through CRM systems and automated nurture sequences. You maintain regular communication via newsletters, relevant job alerts, company updates, and industry content, staying top-of-mind until candidates are ready to explore opportunities. When it works best: Talent communities are essential for competitive talent markets where candidates receive multiple outreach messages and timing matters. They work particularly well for specialized future roles where the candidate pool is small, and you need to build relationships over months or years. Nurture is also effective for passive candidates who expressed interest, but timing wasn't right. Impact and tips: Segment your talent community by role type, skills, or career stage so that nurture content is relevant to each segment. Mix value-added content (industry insights, career advice, company news) with job opportunities. Don't make every message a pitch. Use automation to scale nurture without requiring constant manual effort. Track engagement to identify candidates who are becoming more interested (opening emails more frequently, clicking job links) as signals that they may be ready for outreach strategies. Respect opt-outs immediately; nurture what feels like spam damages your employer brand. 10. Events, meetups, and conferences What it is: In-person and virtual events where you can meet candidates, build relationships, and showcase your company culture. This includes sponsoring industry conferences, hosting technical meetups, attending career fairs, organizing hackathons or design challenges, and running virtual webinars or AMAs. When it works best: Events are most effective for employer brand building and pipeline development rather than immediate hiring. They work particularly well for senior or niche future roles where relationship-building matters, for technical communities with active meetup cultures, and for early-career recruiting, where face-to-face interaction influences decisions. Events also support diversity hiring by connecting with underrepresented communities and affinity groups. Impact and tips: Don't just collect resumes. Focus on building authentic relationships and showcasing what makes your company compelling. Have technical employees attend technical events, not just recruiters; candidates want to meet potential colleagues. Follow up quickly after events while they're still memorable. Track event ROI by immediate applications, and by pipeline adds who convert months later. Consider that smaller, targeted events often deliver better ROI than massive conferences where you're competing with hundreds of other employers. Virtual events can reach broader geographies but lack the depth of relationships found in in-person interaction. 11. Social media and content marketing What it is: Building a passive inbound pipeline through authentic employer brand content on social media. This includes team spotlights and day-in-the-life content, thought leadership from company leaders and employees, behind-the-scenes glimpses of projects and culture, career advice and industry insights, and showcasing company values and impact. When it works best: Social media and content marketing build long-term employer brand awareness that generates passive inbound over time. It's particularly effective in competitive talent markets where candidates research companies thoroughly before applying, in roles where culture fit matters significantly, and for companies seeking to attract candidates aligned with specific values or missions. Impact and tips: Authenticity matters more than polish. Candidates see through overly produced recruiting content. Feature real employees telling real stories rather than corporate marketing speak. Different platforms reach different audiences: LinkedIn for professional roles, Twitter/X for tech and startup communities, Instagram for visual storytelling, TikTok for early-career talent, and other social media platforms. Encourage employees to share their own content about working at your company; peer voices are more credible than official channels. Track which content drives the most engagement and inbound interest. Remember, this is a long-game strategy: social content builds awareness that converts into applications weeks or months later, not immediately. 12. University and early-career pipelines What it is: Building relationships with universities, bootcamps, and training programs to create pipelines for early-career talent. This includes campus recruiting and career fair participation, internship and co-op programs, partnerships with coding bootcamps or design schools, sponsoring student competitions or hackathons, and offering mentorship or guest lectures. When it works best: Early-career pipelines are essential for organizations with significant entry-level hiring needs and those wanting to build diverse talent pools from the ground up. Internship-to-hire programs often deliver the highest quality early-career hires since you've already worked together. This strategy requires long-term investment. Relationships take years to build. Impact and tips: Focus on a core set of schools or programs rather than spreading resources too thin; deep partnerships deliver better results than surface-level engagement at dozens of institutions. Provide meaningful internship experiences with real projects and mentorship. Word spreads quickly among students about which companies offer valuable programs. Engage year-round, not just during recruitment season; sponsor student organizations, offer workshops, or participate in career panels. Track conversion from intern to full-time hire and quality-of-hire to optimize program investment. Consider partnerships with organizations focused on underrepresented groups in tech (e.g., Code2040, Girls Who Code) to build diverse early-career pipelines. How to build a sourcing strategy that works The most effective sourcing strategies combine multiple channels rather than relying on a single approach. Here's how to build a talent sourcing mix that delivers results: Diversify your channel mix. Don't put all your talent sourcing efforts into one channel. LinkedIn outages, algorithm changes, or competitive saturation can suddenly impact performance. Use 4-6 different talent sourcing methods appropriate for your role types and hiring volume. This diversification also improves pipeline diversity, as different channels reach distinct candidate demographics. Measure source effectiveness, not just volume. Track which sources produce hires, not just which generate the most applications. A source producing 100 applications but zero hires is less valuable than one producing 10 applications and 2 hires. Calculate source-to-hire conversion rates, quality-of-hire by source, and time-to-hire by channel. Continuously optimize your mix based on what's actually working. Match channels to role type. Not every sourcing strategy works equally well for every role. Technical roles require sourcing on GitHub and Stack Overflow. Executive roles benefit from relationship-based strategies like events and referrals. High-volume, hourly roles need efficient channels such as targeted job boards and employee referrals. Customize your approach based on what you're hiring for. Balance inbound and outbound. Inbound sourcing (career site, job boards, referrals) is efficient but limited by awareness and interest. Outbound candidate sourcing (AI agents, LinkedIn, multi-channel outreach) proactively reaches passive candidates but requires more effort. The right balance depends on your employer brand strength and the competitiveness of your role. Strong brands can rely more heavily on inbound; companies hiring for competitive roles need robust outbound strategies. Invest in AI to scale without adding headcount. Manual candidate sourcing doesn't scale. There's a limit to how many candidates a recruiter can source, screen, and engage. AI sourcing agents, talent rediscovery, and automated outreach sequences allow you to handle 40%+ more volume without proportionally increasing recruiting team size. This efficiency is essential as application volumes continue rising while recruiting budgets remain constrained. Sourcing metrics to track Measuring qualified talent sourcing effectiveness requires tracking metrics beyond simple application counts: Response rate by channel shows which outreach methods and messaging resonate with candidates. Track email response rates, InMail response rates, and phone pickup rates separately. Benchmark: 15-25% response rates for well-targeted, personalized outreach; under 5% suggests messaging or targeting issues. Source-to-hire conversion reveals which channels drive actual qualified hires rather than just application volume. Calculate what percentage of sourced candidates from each channel ultimately get hired. This helps optimize budget allocation toward the highest-ROI sources. Pipeline diversity by source tracks whether different talent sourcing channels reach diverse candidate pools. This visibility helps you proactively address diversity hiring goals rather than discovering pipeline gaps late in the process. Cost per sourced candidate includes crucial tool costs, recruiter time, and agency fees allocated by channel. This allows for a true ROI comparison across expensive tools like LinkedIn Recruiter and higher-touch, but potentially more effective strategies like events and referrals. Time-to-engage measures how quickly you can move sourced candidates from first contact to application or phone screen. Faster engagement improves conversion since candidates often have multiple opportunities in play. Track delays in your process and optimize accordingly. Ready to scale your candidate sourcing with AI? Gem's sourcing agents search 800M+ profiles, automatically rediscover past candidates for new roles, and integrate with your complete recruiting workflow. Request a demo. FAQ What is the most effective way to source candidates? The most effective talent sourcing approach in your hiring process combines multiple strategies rather than relying on a single channel. However, if forced to prioritize, talent rediscovery (AI surfacing past candidates from your ATS and CRM for new roles) consistently delivers the highest ROI. Forty-six percent of hires at top teams come from existing candidate databases, and these candidates convert faster since they already know your company. Beyond rediscovery, employee referrals typically deliver the highest quality of hire, while AI sourcing agents deliver the best efficiency for scaling outbound efforts without adding recruiting headcount. LinkedIn sourcing remains effective for professional roles, and targeted job boards work well for specialized positions. The key is measuring source effectiveness by conversion to hire rather than just application volume, then continuously optimizing your channel mix based on what actually produces quality hires for your specific role types and company context. How do you source passive candidates? Passive candidates (employed professionals not actively job searching) require proactive outreach rather than job postings. The most effective strategies include AI candidate sourcing agents that search across 800M+ profiles and identify matches based on career trajectory. For technical roles, source on platforms like GitHub and Stack Overflow, where passive candidates are professionally active. Employee referrals also effectively reach passive candidates since your employees can make warm introductions to people in their networks. The key to passive candidate sourcing is personalization — generic mass messages get ignored. Reference specific aspects of their experience, explain why this opportunity aligns with their career trajectory, and provide value beyond just the pitch. Passive candidates are selective, so you need to earn their attention by demonstrating you've actually researched their background and have a relevant opportunity. What is the 80/20 rule in recruiting? The 80/20 rule in recruiting (based on the Pareto Principle) typically refers to the observation that 80% of your quality hires come from 20% of your sourcing channels. This means most recruiting sources generate activity and applications, but only a small subset actually produce hires worth the investment. The implication is to ruthlessly measure source effectiveness and concentrate resources on the highest-performing channels rather than spreading effort equally across all options. Track which sources produce not just applications but actual hires, quality-of-hire by source, and cost-per-hire by channel. Then double down on what's working and eliminate or reduce investment in low-performing sources. For example, you might discover that employee referrals and talent rediscovery produce 80% of your hires despite representing only 20% of applications, suggesting you should invest more in referral programs and AI rediscovery rather than continuing to pay for job boards that generate volume but few hires. The 80/20 rule also applies to recruiter time allocation: 80% of recruiter time often goes to low-value administrative tasks while only 20% goes to high-impact activities like candidate relationships and strategic sourcing. This suggests using AI and automation to handle the 80% of repetitive work, freeing recruiters to focus on the 20% that actually drives hiring success. How to source candidates on LinkedIn for free? Free sourcing strategies include using LinkedIn's standard search with basic filters (location, industry, current company), leveraging your network by searching second and third-degree connections, joining LinkedIn Groups related to your industry or target roles and engaging with active members, using Google X-Ray search to find LinkedIn profiles externally (e.g., "site:linkedin.com/in [keywords] [location]"), and researching company employee pages to find people with target backgrounds. However, free LinkedIn sourcing is constrained : you can't see most profiles outside your network, search results are limited to a few pages, you can't filter by many important criteria like years of experience or skills, and you can't send InMail to candidates outside your network. This makes free LinkedIn sourcing viable only for very occasional hiring or when targeting people in your extended network. For regular sourcing needs, consider alternatives: GitHub is completely free for technical sourcing; many niche job boards offer free basic search; and AI sourcing platforms like Gem often deliver better ROI than managing multiple sourcing licenses by searching across 800M+ profiles from multiple sources, at a lower cost.

title: Dailybot | We're launching Dailybot 3, the coordination layer for people-agent teams · Changelog
summary: Software teams are no longer just people. Dailybot 3 is the intelligence layer for teams where people and AI agents work side by side, with agent check-ins, proactive insights, and the infrastructure agents need to be real team members.
body_text: Dailybot 3.0 · April 2026 Software teams aren’t just people anymore Something changed in the way software gets built. Coding agents crossed a threshold. They can now reason through complex, multi-step tasks, break them down on their own, execute across multiple passes, and review their own output. What used to take a developer a full day can now be delegated to an agent that works for hours and delivers production-ready code. In practice, it feels closer to the leap the personal computer introduced. A new kind of computing that can develop itself, choose its own tools, and operate at a pace we didn’t think possible. The teams building software today aren’t made up of people alone anymore. They’re people and agents, side by side. And yet, all that agent work is invisible. A developer runs an agent for three hours, a dozen files change, and the standup is still blank. The manager doesn’t know what happened. The team can’t see the blockers. The agent sits idle, waiting for feedback nobody knows it needs. Dailybot 3 is built for this reality. What Dailybot 3 is Dailybot started as a way to help teams stay coordinated. Async standups, blocker detection, recognition, escalation workflows. That was built for teams of people. Dailybot 3 extends those same capabilities to the full team, people and agents together. It’s the platform where you can see what your entire team is doing and get actionable insights about what needs to happen next. Not a dashboard you have to visit. Not a chart you have to interpret. An intelligence layer that picks up on what matters and brings it to you, before you knew to ask. We’re not a project management tool. We’re not an HR analytics platform. Your Linear and Jira still track tasks. Dailybot tells you your team is blocked on infrastructure before you ever open a dashboard. That’s a different category. You’ll notice everything looks different too. The website, the brand, the product design. We rebuilt it all because Dailybot 3 isn’t an update to what came before, and we wanted the experience to reflect that. Why we rebuilt the brand Dailybot started as a daily standup bot. The name said it all. But the product outgrew that a long time ago. It became a coordination layer, an intelligence surface, a system that connects people and agents across an entire organization. The brand needed to catch up. We asked ourselves a simple question: what is the smallest unit of work, of presence, of signal? The answer was a dot. A single point. Minimal, neutral, full of potential. That dot became the foundation of the new identity. It represents something that can evolve, adapt, and take different forms — just like Dailybot. Because Dailybot isn’t one fixed assistant. It’s a system that shapes itself around your team, your tools, and the way you work. The design language follows the same principle. Black, white, and grayscale. Not just an aesthetic choice — it creates calm. In a world of constant dashboards, notification badges, and blinking status lights, removing visual noise is a feature. Clarity is the product, so clarity had to be the brand. Everything Dailybot does comes down to turning raw signals — from people, agents, APIs, GitHub, Linear, Jira, and more — into something you can understand and act on. The new identity reflects that: strip away the noise, surface what matters. Agent check-ins and automatic standup population New When a coding agent finishes a session, Dailybot picks it up and fills in the developer’s standup. People updates and agent updates show up side by side in the same feed. No one has to type a thing. This matters because agent work is invisible work. A solid job that nobody can see is a job that gets questioned. Dailybot makes agent contributions visible, trustworthy, and part of the team’s shared record. Agents report activity and health status the same way people submit standups, and both show up together in one feed. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, and any agent that uses the Dailybot CLI. AI attribution gets stored as metadata, so the standup stays clean and readable while the full picture is always available underneath. New Home, proactive intelligence New The redesigned Home surface brings information to you instead of making you go find it. Instead of opening a dashboard and scrolling through charts, you see what actually matters. Your team is blocked today because of an infrastructure dependency. Three agents are waiting on a decision. Here’s what needs to happen next. That’s intelligence. That’s what project management tools don’t do. That’s the category we’re building. The unified feed shows people standups and agent reports together. Blocker detection is proactive, so problems surface before you have to ask. There’s an agent health view that shows each agent’s last report time, current status, and what it’s working on. AI-generated insights summarize context across the whole team. And for larger orgs, enterprise analytics break down people vs. agent work contributions and how they trend over time. Agent infrastructure New For agents to work well alongside people, they need more than a reporting endpoint. They need an identity, a way to communicate, a way to flag when they’re stuck, and a way to know who to ask. Communication is existential for agents. Transparency is how they earn trust, and trust is how they keep running. Think of it like a fleet. Every hour an agent sits idle waiting for feedback is time and money lost. Dailybot sits in the middle, making the handoff between people and agents as fast and smooth as possible. Right now, every agent gets a dedicated email address for communicating with people and other agents, even outside your org. There’s a structured progress reporting mechanism that’s visible to the whole team in the shared feed. When an agent hits a blocker, Dailybot routes it to the right person immediately. Team awareness, where agents can look up who’s on their team and who to ask for specific decisions, is in progress. Automations rebuilt for speed Improved Every hour an agent spends idle waiting on a decision is a bottleneck you can fix. The rebuilt automation engine is designed to keep decisions flowing. Fast handoffs between people and agents, no pile-ups. A new no-code gallery lets you install templates in seconds. Three new templates ship with this release. Hybrid Standup creates a single report that combines people and agent updates for the whole team. Agent Heartbeat sends an automated health pulse for long-running agents, so you always know they’re still going. And Incident Intake provides a structured triage flow for platform and DevOps teams. Kudos in the unified feed Improved When agents take on more of the execution, recognizing the people who make the judgment calls matters more, not less. Kudos is now a first-class feature in the unified feed. It shows up in Home right alongside standups and agent reports, with an improved modal experience across Slack, Google Chat, Discord, and MS Teams. Recognition data is also included in the leadership digest and analytics, so it doesn’t just feel good. It gets tracked. Developer API and CLI New If agents find genuine value in Dailybot, the people managing them will follow. That starts with making Dailybot easy for any agent to connect to, and discoverable by agents on their own. Agents can now register directly through POST /v1/agent/register/ without needing Slack OAuth or any chat platform at all. People can create named agent identities from their dashboard using people-sponsored tokens. New CLI commands like dailybot agent report and dailybot agent inbox give agents the tools to report, check instructions, and submit health signals. Developer docs include Claude Code and Cursor examples with Q&A sections. And Dailybot publishes machine-readable surfaces — agent-card.json , agent-skills/index.json , llms.txt , llms-full.txt — so agents can discover the API, the skill pack, and the auth handshake without a human in the loop. On top of the CLI and API, we’re releasing an open-source agent skill pack that any coding agent can install in one step. It gives agents four native capabilities — reporting progress, checking for team messages, sending emails, and announcing health status. One git clone , one setup script, and the agent knows how to use Dailybot without any extra prompting. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Cline, and Gemini CLI. What’s ahead We’re at the beginning of something. The teams building software right now are the first generation where people and agents share the same standup, the same feed, the same blockers. The pilot still matters. Skilled people make agents produce their best work. But the direction is clear, and every team will work this way. Dailybot 3 is the coordination layer for that future. Everything you had is still here. Everything new is ready.

title: Productivity isn’t a luxury
summary: For many of us, productivity is no longer a luxury. It's the best way to make sure your limited time actually works for you.
body_text: When you’re feeling overwhelmed, productivity is usually the first thing to go. It’s not (usually) because you don’t care, but because it feels like too much. Trying to optimize your time or follow a system when you’re barely keeping your head above water sounds ridiculous. So when you hit that wall, you check out and focus on what’s right in front of you. The problem is that opting out of productivity makes everything worse, not better. All of your responsibilities continue to pile up, whether you’ve got a plan or not. But without a plan for your time, they’re much harder to manage. At one time or another, we’ve all been at that point. Maybe your company just had a round of layoffs, so you’re dealing with an increased workload plus job insecurity. Maybe finances are tight, so you’ve had to work for side income during nights and weekends. Or maybe you’re just busy balancing full-time work with parenting and all the responsibilities that come with being an adult. Although everyone’s experience is unique, feeling overwhelmed isn’t, and there are steps we can take to try to limit it. It’s time we take back the narrative surrounding productivity. Let’s talk about a new way to look at productivity and how we can manage our time to prevent reaching total burnout. The reality: Your time is still being spent, with or without intentionality Time is, by far, our most finite resource. Even if you’re not actively managing your time, your day is still passing. But without a solid plan for your time, the hours get filled with time-wasters that do nothing to move you forward. If we look at this concept through the lens of the Eisenhower Matrix , it often means we’re spending a lot of time in the not urgent/not important quadrant or the urgent/not important quadrant. ​ While it might feel like you’re opting out of productivity when you start to get overwhelmed, what’s really happening is that you’re opting out of deciding how your time is used. When you reach this point, your time defaults to the path of least resistance. That can look like: cleaning out your inbox responding to the most recent request instead of the most critical filling small gaps in your day with low-effort, low-impact work saying yes to every meeting without considering whether your attendance is necessary None of these things looks particularly harmful in the moment. They might even seem productive. But over the course of a week, they can insidiously take over until your best hours are consumed by reactive work. Soon, you feel like you’re busy all day, but you don’t have much to show for all the hours you spent in front of your screen. You’re tired, but you never reach a point of being done for the day. Learn how to view productivity as control, not output Unfortunately, productivity has become synonymous with output. Our culture tells us that being productive equals getting more done in less time. On the surface, that sounds ideal. Who wouldn’t want to be more efficient? But experience is quick to teach us that this view of productivity ends up making productivity feel like pressure. It turns your to-do list into a measuring stick, and no matter how much you accomplish, there’s always more you could be doing. That’s when productivity starts to feel like pressure . When you look at productivity this way, being productive means pushing harder, working longer, and trying to optimize every minute of your day. And when you’re already overwhelmed, that expectation just adds another layer of stress. But that’s the wrong lens. A more useful way to think about productivity is this: it’s a tool for control. Control over your time and control over your attention. Most of us aren’t dealing with a lack of effort as much as a lack of clarity. We haven’t taken the time to name what matters and map that out to the time we have available. As a result, our day gets shaped by other people’s priorities more than our own. When you shift your view of productivity from output to control, the way you view your to-do list and your schedule starts to change. Instead of asking how you can get more done, you begin to ask what actually deserves your time and attention. This change in mindset helps you make better decisions and make the best use of the time you have. What happens when you don’t track your time I can’t possibly be the only person who has sat down for a 10-minute social media break, only to be shocked when I realize almost an hour has passed. For most humans, our perception of time is easily skewed. It’s easy to make assumptions about how you spend your workday, so without concrete data and plans, you can end up wasting time on work that isn’t very meaningful or underestimating how much time you need to complete a certain project. Soon, everything starts to blur together. You feel busy, but it’s hard to pinpoint what you actually accomplished. You can end up spending too much time on reactive tasks, while more important tasks get pushed farther and farther down the road. And when you feel like you’re always behind, the natural response is to push harder. You work longer days and stay ‘on’ all the time. Talk about a recipe for burnout. On the flip side, tracking your time and using that data to map out your day is essential if you want to stop feeling like you’re perpetually behind. The initial time and effort it takes pales in comparison to the time and effort it saves you in the long run. Four ways to use time tracking to reduce burnout We tend to have a narrow view of burnout, seeing it simply as the product of working too many hours. The reality is that burnout happens when you spend your time in ways that drain you without moving anything forward. Here are four ways you can use time tracking to conserve your energy and reclaim your time: Cut low-value work Time tracking quickly shows you how much of your day is spent on tasks that don’t meaningfully contribute to your goals, like unnecessary meetings, busywork, and instant communication. Once you start to identify all of the interrupters that are keeping you from meeting your actual goals at work, you can start looking at ways to eliminate them. The kind of low-value work you can cut often comes in the form of: over-formatting content low-impact admin work unnecessary communication multitasking during deep work Say goodbye to these tasks and the stress they add to your day. Protect focus time One of the main reasons for burnout is that you’re constantly changing contexts . With the never-ending stream of notifications coming from our tech tools, we’re lucky to get 20 minutes of uninterrupted focus time these days. It’s hard to make meaningful progress when you get off track every 10 minutes. Time tracking helps you pinpoint when your focus is strongest so you can take intentional steps to protect that time. If you hadn’t noticed by now, we’re really into Focus Sessions at RescueTime. It’s why they’re such an important feature of the app, making it easier to cancel out all the other noise and hone in on important work. Block it off on your calendar. Protect it from meetings. Keep your phone in the other room. Do whatever you need to do to give yourself the gift of an uninterrupted work session where you actually reach your goal. Make smarter tradeoffs Another big contributor to burnout? Trying to do everything at once. Do you remember seeing this meme in college? ​ ​ As a 20-year-old, I laughed at the accuracy. Now, as a working adult with several kids, I think I’d need a decagon to include all of the factors I need to balance. Within my work as a freelance writer, I’m trying to balance work for several different clients, my own perfectionism, the admin side of my business, online marketing to keep myself relevant, pitching to new clients to maintain a pipeline, et cetera, et cetera. And as a working mom, that work balance is always impacted by my parenting responsibilities—running kids to and from school, staying home for sick days, and anticipating school breaks. It’s a lot of spinning plates to keep in the air at once, and I know I’m not alone in this regard. There’s just no way to do it all perfectly all the time. Anyone who tells you they are is fooling themselves or working themselves to the point of physical and mental collapse. When you’re determining what to trade off, use the rubber ball/glass ball theory . Some tasks can be dropped for the time being, and they’ll bounce back for later. Other tasks will shatter if you let them go, so they’re what you need to prioritize and keep a close eye on. Give yourself some breathing room Sometimes, a lack of productivity is caused by distractions. But there’s another cause that we tend to ignore: our brains are simply too tired. When you’re trying to work 50-60 hours, week after week, your body and mind begin to feel the strain. Pushing yourself to the breaking point, without allowing yourself adequate rest, puts you on the fast track to burnout . Time tracking gives you an accurate snapshot of how your time is being spent, which can be useful for: showing you exactly how many hours you’ve spent working (especially when you tend to underestimate) revealing patterns of when you’re more and less productive Those two datasets can help you understand when you need to take a break because you’ve exceeded a healthy number of working hours or your brain needs a quick reset before it’s ready to function at optimal levels. A healthier way to think about productivity In today’s always-on culture, productivity has gotten a bad rap, and it’s not hard to see why. Work can feel endless, and the world outside of work feels just as heavy, making the idea of ‘ being more productive ’ sound exhausting. When people resist the idea of productivity, it’s not that they don’t care. It’s that they’re already stretched thin. They don’t want ways to do more; they want ways to cope with what’s currently going on. That’s where sustainable, human-centered productivity comes in. We have to start viewing productivity as something that protects us. As much as I hate to admit it sometimes, I thrive when I monitor my time and follow a planned schedule. I hit all my deadlines early. I get adequate sleep so I can enjoy a clear head. My house stays orderly (at least, as much as it can when twin toddlers are living here). We think that increasing productivity = squeezing as much work out of yourself as possible. But that’s not what sustainable productivity looks like. When you learn how to improve your productivity to better control your day, you are able to complete the work that actually matters and reclaim the time you were wasting on all those unnecessary tasks. You also gain the ability to recognize your limits and set firm boundaries. It becomes more obvious when work is creeping into your personal time, allowing you to make adjustments before it turns into long-term burnout. You don’t have to rely on your gut to manage your time, because you have actual data to guide your decisions. We all have a lot on our plates right now. Being mindful about how we manage our time is key.

title: Toro Corp. Declares Special Dividend of $0.90 Per Share
summary: LIMASSOL, Cyprus, April 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Toro Corp. (NASDAQ: TORO) (“Toro”, or the “Company”), a global energy transportation provider, today...
body_text: LIMASSOL, Cyprus, April 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Toro Corp. (NASDAQ: TORO) (“Toro”, or the “Company”), a global energy transportation provider, today announced that the Company's board of directors has declared a one-time, special dividend of $0.90 per common share, consisting of either cash or the Company’s common shares. The dividend is payable to the Company’s shareholders of record at the close of business on May 4, 2026 and is expected to be paid on June 5, 2026 (the “Dividend Payment Date”). The Company expects the dividend will be a taxable dividend to shareholders, regardless of whether received in the form of cash or common shares. For shareholders that wish to receive the dividend all in cash, no further action is required . Alternatively, shareholders can elect to receive the dividend all in common shares. The number of common shares issued as a result of the dividend will be based on the 20-day volume weighted average price through April 21, 2026 (“20-day VWAP”) of the Company’s common shares, which the Company has determined is equal to $3.8821 per share. The market value of shares received on the Dividend Payment Date may be greater or less than the 20-day VWAP. The Company reserves the right to determine, at any time up to midnight on June 4, 2026, to pay the dividend entirely in cash, notwithstanding any elections it has received and without prior notice to shareholders. An information letter and election form will be mailed to shareholders of record after the record date. The properly completed election form must be received by Broadridge Corporate Issuer Solutions, LLC, the Company's transfer agent, prior to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on May 22, 2026. If the transfer agent does not receive a valid election form from a shareholder by that time, the dividend on such shareholder’s shares will be paid in cash. Registered shareholders with questions regarding the dividend election may call Broadridge Corporate Issuer Solutions, LLC at (888) 789-8409. Shareholders who hold their shares through a bank, broker or nominee and have questions regarding the dividend election should contact such bank, broker or nominee, who will also be responsible for distributing to them the information letter and election form and submitting the election form on their behalf. About Toro Corp. Toro Corp. is a global energy transportation services provider, operating a modern fleet of oceangoing vessels. The Company’s fleet comprises two LPG carriers, and two MR tanker vessels, transporting petrochemical gases and refined petroleum products worldwide. Toro is incorporated under the laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The Company's common shares trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol “TORO”.
